newsitem.title: USA: U.S. credit card delinquencies level off in Q1-ABA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. credit card delinquencies level off in Q1-ABA.

text.p: A rapid rise in credit card delinquencies halted in the first quarter, as 3.51 percent of all credit accounts paid late compared to 3.53 percent in the first quarter of 1996, American Bankers Association reported.
The seasonally adjusted Q1 figure was also down from 3.72 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, the banking group said.

But the dollar amount of late payments rose to 5.43 percent in the first quarter from 4.62 percent a year earlier when measured in terms of total loans outstanding and without a seasonal adjustment. The dollar amount of late payments was 5.45 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.

"It may have stopped raining but there are still clouds in the sky," ABA's chief economist James Chessen said. "Banks have adjusted their credit standards to bring delinquencies in line but more tightening may be needed."

Delinquency rates on other types of consumer were mixed, the group said. About 1.38 percent of home equity loan accounts had late payments in Q1, down from 1.44 percent a year earlier and 1.42 percent in the previous quarter.
On direct auto loans, 2.10 percent seasonally adjusted of all accounts paid late in the first quarter, up from 1.74 percent a year earlier and 2.03 percent the previous quarter.
On indirect car loans, 2.55 percent seasonally adjusted of all accounts paid late in the first quarter, up from 2.13 percent a year earlier and 2.36 percent the previous quarter.
The group's seasonally adjusted composite consumer loan figure rose to 2.47 percent of all accounts in the first quarter, up from 2.14 percent a year earlier and 2.34 in the previous quarter.
In dollar terms, not seasonally adjusted, the composite delinquency rate hit 1.95 percent in the first quarter, up from 1.66 percent a year earlier but down from 2.13 percent the previous quarter.
The composite figure is comprised of auto, personal, home equity, home improvement, recreational vehicle, mobile home and marine loans.
The ABA delinquency rates are based on a survey of over 500 banks and count loan payments 30 days or more overdue as delinquent.
